messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: evaluation synthesis, recommended pins & rollback criteria

Hi Jules / Alkemy team — thanks again for the run-through today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

- Key success criteria: (1) classification precision on support triage >= 92% on your validation set, (2) median latency < 220ms p50 in your eu-west region for 2k daily concurrent users, (3) strict PII retention rules in audit logs.
- Primary narrow use-cases: ticket triage + suggested resolution snippets (short form), and automated first-touch classification routing (labels + confidence).
- Concerns you raised: model consistency after updates (esp. phrasing changes), and procurement timelines for a Dedicated pool.

Immediate next steps agreed:
1) We’ll send an evaluation pack (benchmark reports, recommended model variants, and curated prompt sets) by EOD tomorrow.
2) We’ll propose pin criteria and a rollback playbook to avoid regressions after any model/version update.
3) We’ll provide an estimated Dedicated capacity quote and procurement checklist to your procurement mailbox.

Attachments: alkemy_poc_scope.pdf (pdf) — scope & acceptance criteria (from today’s call).

Let me know if I missed anything. I’ll follow up with the evaluation assets + links.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

pri y om@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0172

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Jules Martin <jules@alkemytech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: evaluation synthesis, recommended pins & rollback criteria

Thanks Jules — appreciate the prompt follow-up and the questionnaire — received and archived. Below is the evaluation synthesis and the actions we recommend for a low-risk pilot: 

What we’re sending (links below):
- Benchmark report (Alkemy sample vs. Redwood baselines) — highlights: redwood/conv-lite-1.2 has highest latency headroom but shows occasional hallucination on rare entity-normalization prompts; open-x-70b-q4f gives the cleanest text consistency at slightly higher cost.
- Curated prompt set with negative cases (prompt-sets/alkemy/2026-11) — includes 120 test prompts modeled on your tickets and 30 synthetic adversarial phrasings.
- Diff report (model v1.2 -> v1.3) — short summary of tokenization differences and 12 failing examples where generation brevity changed tone.

Recommended model variants and pin strategy (pilot):
- Start pilot on redwood/conv-lite-1.2@rev-20260914 for triage (cost-efficient, fast).
- Use open-x-70b-q4f@rev-20261001 for suggestion snippets where tone consistency matters.
- Set automatic pin fallback: if weekly regression rate on the prompt-set (weighted by severity) exceeds 4%, auto-pin traffic to last-known-good pinned revision and trigger a rollback runbook.

Suggested rollback/runbook criteria (technical ops):
- Regression signal: >4% failing prompts on the 150-item canonical set OR >7% increase in low-confidence labels (score < 0.55) vs baseline.
- Latency SLO breach: sustained p50 > 320ms for 15 minutes (for a Dedicated pilot target of p50 < 220ms).
- Action: (1) automatic traffic split rollback to pinned rev; (2) notify AE + CS + Infra on-call; (3) spin up compatibility test suite against new candidate revision.

Assets and links: 
- Benchmark & diff report: https://redwood.gdrive/alkemy/benchmarks/2026-11-05
- Prompt sets: https://redwood.gdrive/alkemy/prompt-sets
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/D-34988

Attachments referenced: alkemy_benchmark_summary.pdf (pdf) — included in GDrive pack.

Notes on evidence of regression causes: our analysis flags two common causes for wording drift after updates — (A) tokenization changes / BPE merges affecting punctuation handling, and (B) decoder sampling temperature defaults tweaked in some quantized builds. Engineering can usually resolve by aligning the tokenizer config and re-running a short constrained fine-tune or adjusting decoding defaults.

Next steps we propose:
1) Your team to run the prompt-set and confirm acceptance criteria (we can run on your sample if you prefer).
2) We’ll provision a short-term Dedicated pilot quote for the capacity you specified and include emergency pinning on the control plane.
3) If you want, we can add a pre-deploy canary stage that evaluates 500 random production-like requests before a wide rollout.

If these recommendations look good I’ll loop in Solutions Engineering to finalize the rollback thresholds and ask Markus to approve the emergency pin margin.

Best,
Priyom

Looping in a quick engineering note and request for approval: 

- Engineering read: the diff report correctly surfaces tokenizer merges that explain 9 of the 12 failing examples. For pilot safety we recommend pinning both model revs (triage & snippet) to the specified revisions and enabling the canonical prompt-set smoke test to run nightly against the pilot traffic.
- Operational ask: we need manager approval to enable the emergency auto-pin fallback (it can be turned off after pilot stabilization). This will briefly reserve additional headroom for a read-only pinned fallback and raise cost by ~6% during rollbacks.

@Markus — can you approve the emergency auto-pin setting for Alkemy pilot (deal D-34988)? If approved, I’ll schedule the canary and ensure alerts + runbook are wired to Infra on-call.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
